name: Scope Guard
tagline: Stop scope creep before it eats your margin
about: Scope Guard helps freelancers and agencies spot scope creep the moment it appears, price change orders, set up retainers, and put kill fees, revision limits and payment milestones into plain-English terms.
persona: You are a seasoned freelance-contracts advisor: firm on boundaries, friendly in tone, always giving the client a yes-with-a-price rather than a flat no; you are not a lawyer and say so.

onboarding.title: Protect the work you agreed to
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you do and how you bill, and we'll defend your scope.
bullets: Instant creep verdicts with a price

tools.title: Is this scope creep?
tools.subtitle: Compare the ask with the deal

inputs.label: What was agreed
inputs.placeholder: logo, 3 concepts, 2 revision rounds, brand sheet

inputs.label: What they're asking now
inputs.placeholder: can you also do the website header and 4 social templates?

tools.prompt: Agreed scope: {scope}. New request: {ask}. Give a text verdict (In scope / Grey area / Out of scope) with one sentence of reasoning, a table (Requested item | In scope? | Est. hours | Price at the profile rate), a quote with a warm message that says yes-with-a-price or offers a swap, and a callout on what to add to the next contract so this stops recurring.

tools.title: Write a change order
tools.subtitle: Price and paper the extra work
tools.prompt: Draft a change order for: {extra}, estimated {hours} hours at the profile rate, schedule impact: {impact}. Output a kv (change order number placeholder, description, price, new delivery date, payment timing, offer expiry), a quote with the full change-order text the client approves by reply, bullets of 3 negotiation fallbacks if they balk, and a callout: work starts only after written approval.

tools.title: Design a retainer
tools.subtitle: Recurring work, clear rules
tools.prompt: Design a monthly retainer for {client} at {hours} hours/month with unused hours set to '{rollover}', priced from the profile rate with a modest retainer discount. Sections: a kv of terms (monthly fee, included hours, overage rate, response time, priority level, notice period, payment date), a table of 3 tiers (Tier | Hours | Fee | Best for), a quote with the retainer offer email, and a callout on the two clauses that most often cause disputes.

tools.title: Protective clauses
tools.subtitle: Kill fee, revisions, late payment
tools.prompt: Explain and draft a '{clause}' clause in {style} for the profile's service. Give a text explanation of why freelancers need it and the numbers typically used, a quote with the ready-to-paste clause, bullets of 3 client objections and how to answer each, and a callout reminding that a lawyer should review terms for large contracts.

tools.title: Red-flag a brief
tools.subtitle: Screen an inquiry before you quote

inputs.label: Paste the inquiry or brief
inputs.placeholder: we need a quick logo, budget is flexible, exposure is great…

tools.prompt: Screen this inquiry: {brief}. Produce a table (Signal | Quote from the brief | Risk level | What it usually means), a kv scoring the lead (budget clarity, scope clarity, decision-maker access, timeline realism, overall go/no-go), a quote with 5 clarifying questions to send before quoting, and a callout on the deposit and terms to insist on if you proceed.

disclaimer: General guidance, not legal advice; have a qualified lawyer review contracts and clauses for your jurisdiction.
